title.title: SAM lane calibration in the bowling engine: before vs after
title.sub: 2026-09-13 engine-integration loop, Tom's Gym bowling analysis
lines: Five research loops (2026-09-12/13) found how to locate the lane to a board or better:
SAM 2 prompted with three points along the ball path on a clean pre-hit frame, a far-end crop pass,
the standing pin rack as a far-end ruler, and one calibrated lane carried per frame through a camera model.
This loop ships that recipe as one pass of the engine (--sam-lane) and measures the deployed
engine against it on the three annotated videos, with the loops' own metric.

method.title: What changed in the engine
method.sub: worktree lane-engine, branch feat/sam-lane-calibration; the old engine is the deployed lineage (situp-config)
lines: BEFORE: one static lane per video from classical anchor detection (foul line, gutters, pins) before the ball is tracked;
boards come from the ball's x between that lane's edges. A handheld phone drifts 24-36 px over a throw: 10+ boards at the pins.
AFTER (pass 5, after tracking): the ball path prompts SAM 2 tiny on pin-hit minus 4 frames -> the mask component holding the prompts
-> one robust line per edge; a second SAM pass on a crop of the far 55 % of the lane re-samples the pin end;
the pin rack is fitted from that lane and, when it passes its gate, a metric homography from foul corners + 10 pin bases;
ORB + RANSAC similarity per frame carries the lane to every frame; boards are recomputed; the debug video is re-rendered.
Metric (loops 1-4): the annotated ball path on each frame mapped to boards through the engine's lane vs the truth lane; board MAE.
Truth = loop 4's pins-based corners (the hand corners are 1-2 boards off at the pins). Chardie needs the engine's YOLO ball detector
to get any track (0 % without it), so the AFTER runs use --yolo; the lane metric uses the annotated path, so it is detector-independent.

results.title: Board MAE of the ball path through the engine's lane, per frame of the throw (pins truth)
results.sub: median over throw frames; <=2 boards = share of frames within two boards; final board = the engine's product number
note: Before = deployed config (--simple-detect). After = --simple-detect --yolo --sam-lane (far-end crop on, pin rack off: from the SAM lane it finds the one-column alias).
Truth final board = annotated ball at pin hit under the pins-based lane. Chardie's after-number is capped by the tracker losing the ball at frame 108 of 134.

end.title: What to do with it
lines: The pass is behind --sam-lane (service: SAM_LANE=1). Deploying it needs torch + ultralytics in the service image and the
78 MB sam2.1_t weights; the service reads final_board / entry_board / lane_edges from summary.json. Ship --yolo with it.
Every stage degrades to the previous one: no weights, no mask, every candidate frame rejected -> the old lane and boards stand.
Real tracker output needed four gates the research never did: the rolling segment, candidates past the track's end,
the mask must reach the path's far end, and it must be static across two frames (a bowler's legs pass everything else).
Left out: the pin-rack refit (finds the one-column alias from the SAM lane), the seg student, SAM video mode, the alley face.
